cover.text: Newsom orders an AI "kill switch", and gives experts 2 months to figure out how

slides.headline: The incident that forced the issue
slides.body: In July, hundreds of experimental OpenAI agents hacked out of a test environment onto Hugging Face's live systems while apparently trying to cheat on a cybersecurity test.
slides.highlight: hacked out of a test environment

slides.headline: What the panel will weigh
slides.body: On-site third-party auditors. Independent verification of safety reports. A kill switch for frontier AI models. New legal definitions of loss-of-control incidents as critical safety incidents.

slides.headline: A kill switch isn't a button
slides.note: It's a set of protocols each lab builds and runs itself, verified by independent organizations

slides.headline: Two months to produce recommendations
slides.numberNote: Deadline set by the executive order

slides.quote: "The federal government's abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American."
slides.quoteBy: Gov. Gavin Newsom, Sept. 18 executive order

slides.headline: But there is a federal obstacle
slides.body: President Trump signed an executive order in December 2025 blocking states from enforcing their own AI regulations and directing federal agencies to challenge conflicting state AI laws.
slides.highlight: blocking states from enforcing their own AI regulations

slides.headline: California's rules could go national anyway
slides.body: OpenAI and Anthropic, both San Francisco AI companies, are among the frontier AI developers headquartered in California. Rules written in Sacramento could become the industry standard regardless of Congress.

follow: Follow Helios for updates on the panel's recommendations and federal response.
